title: M8 confirmatory parameter-specific optimal-design benchmark
scope: Controlled synthetic evaluation of parameter-specific identifiability and measurement design using HydroSheaf's production transport and kinetic calibration adapters; no field-validation claim is permitted.

objectives.statement: Quantify dispersivity and decay recovery separately across controlled transport sampling designs.
acceptance_criteria: Report parameter-specific log-error, uncertainty coverage, and paired bootstrap intervals.
Use a noise-whitened Jacobian in log10-parameter space.
Do not infer significance by treating deterministic sampling designs as random observations.

objectives.statement: Test whether target-specific and joint Fisher-information criteria select different next observations and whether their predicted advantages transfer to realised recovery.
acceptance_criteria: Use common random numbers and common starting values across strategies.
Compare parameter-targeted, D-, A-, E-, balanced, random, redundant, and no-new-measurement strategies.
Separate local-start performance from distant-start sensitivity.

objectives.statement: Verify the structural k-times-surface-area non-identifiability in the production PHREEQC kinetic adapter and test an independent surface-area constraint as the identifying intervention.
acceptance_criteria: Use the production KineticCalibrationAdapter and PHREEQC forward calculation.
Demonstrate constant-product ridge invariance and a rank-one data-only Fisher matrix.
Show that an independent surface-area observation restores full local rank.

inputs.provenance: HydroSheaf checkout containing production transport and kinetic adapters

risks.risk: Raw-parameter Fisher metrics depend on parameter units.
risks.mitigation: Differentiate with respect to log10 parameters and whiten by the declared observation error model.

risks.risk: Random starting values can become random regularisation centres.
risks.mitigation: Disable adapter-created priors for the primary data-identifiability experiment.

risks.risk: Previously inspected exploratory results cannot be retrospectively preregistered.
risks.mitigation: Use a new locked protocol, fresh run ID, and fresh seed family; label the result prospective confirmation.
